subject.title: codex app-server drops guardianWarning on rejection circuit-breaker interrupts

question: Should this maintainer-labeled Codex app-server guardian warning bug be promoted now to a focused fix PR, and should the warning be surfaced as an agent event, terminal metadata, or both?
rationale: The bug is source-backed and narrow, but the protected label prevents automated cleanup or repair without maintainer intent, and the final user-visible sink is an owner-boundary choice.

options.title: Promote Focused Projector Fix
options.body: Handle `guardianWarning` in the Codex app-server projector, preserve the message in both diagnostics and terminal-result metadata if feasible, and add the focused interrupted-turn regression.

options.title: Require Live Circuit-Breaker Proof First
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer captures a live guardian rejection-limit trace that proves the exact downstream user-visible failure.

options.title: Limit To Diagnostic Event
options.body: Preserve the warning only as a diagnostic/agent event and defer terminal metadata until a channel-specific user-visible requirement is proven.

recommendation.title: Promote Focused Projector Fix
recommendation.body: Handle `guardianWarning` in the Codex app-server projector, preserve the message in both diagnostics and terminal-result metadata if feasible, and add the focused interrupted-turn regression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent maintainer stack guidance on Codex app-server terminalization makes this the best available owner for the projection contract choice.
